(2) Insurance Contracts. Although the prevalence of oppressive "take 
it or leave it" clauses has increased in recent years, insurance contracts have 
traditionally been a rich source for the regulation of adhesion contracts. In 
Darner Motor Sales v. Universal Underwriters, 682 P.2d 388, 399 (Ariz. 
1984), the court applied the Restatement 
provision to the terms of an 
"umbrella" insurance policy favorably to the insured. It characterized the 
policy as one which, "because of the nature of the enterprise, customers will 
not be expected to read and over which they have no real power of 
negotiation." Another technique used to overcome terms that have literally
